title: the carrier of every scope and the file that holds it
intent: The wave is the second of the track C of the catch-up plan (the areas of the approval).  Wave C1 named the scope of an answer and refused by name a scope that has no carrier -- but the table of the carriers was a list of names and the place where a rule of a scope really lives was decided in three different places: the rules of the process, the rules of an attached run and the rules of an ACP session, and the scopes `:project' and `:global' had no place at all.  The repair gives every scope of the dictionary exactly one carrier, and the correspondence lives in one table (`yeah-perm--carriers' in `lib/yeah-perm.el'): the scope `once' is the scope of the call itself and holds no rule -- a rule that carries it is refused by name, because a rule that lives nowhere is not a rule; the scope `run' is held by the memory of the run; the scope `session' is held by the memory of the ACP session; the scope `project' is held by the file `.yeah/rules.json' of the project; the scope `global' is held by the file `yeah/rules.json' of the configuration of the user (`$XDG_CONFIG_HOME', and the home directory when the variable of the environment is not set).  A rule of a scope is written into the carrier of that scope and into no other, and the three paths that write a rule -- the person, the run and the session -- were changed to ask the one rule instead of deciding for themselves.  The format of the file is JSON, a list of objects with the fields `action', `resource', `effect' and `scope'; a file that is not there is a file of no rules and not an error, a file that is broken is a refusal that names the file and the reason, and the write is atomic: the rules go into a temporary file of the same directory and the temporary file takes the place of the file, so a reader never sees half of it.  The rules of the files and the rules of the process decide together: the files come first (the broadest carrier first, the narrowest last) and the rules of the process come last, because they are the freshest.  The claim of the wave is new (`a-scope-decides-where-the-rule-lives').
objection: What the wave does not prove, and its price is named.  (a) **A scope is still one kind of thing**: the scope `run' and the scope `session' are both held in the memory of a path and differ only in who owns the memory; a person who answers 'always' in the attached path and in the service path writes into two different places, and the wave names both without unifying them -- that is the wave C3, which gives the surfaces the four scopes of the document.  (b) **The plain answerer is the global path**: an answer that the shared view produces in a process that is neither a run nor a session writes into the file of the user, and the file of the user is now a file on the disk of the person; the wave gave the kernel a knob (`yeah-perm-config-home') so that a check may keep its rules in a directory of its own, but the default is the configuration of the user and the person is not asked before the first write.  (c) **The rules of the process are not the carrier of a scope**: the rules that the process holds in its memory are freshest and decide last, and the scope `global' is the file of the user and not the memory of the process -- the two live apart and the wave does not merge them.  (d) **The file of the project is written by the kernel and not asked for**: the file `.yeah/rules.json' of the project is created by the answer that names the scope `project', and the wave does not ask the person whether the project may hold such a file.  (e) **A broken file refuses everything**: a rules file that cannot be read stops the computation of the permission instead of being ignored, and a person whose file is broken is refused every call until the file is fixed -- the wave names this price and does not soften it.  (f) **The wave found a defect of a check that was not its own**: the check of the approvals (`check-approvals-have-reply-kinds.el') wrote a rule of the scope `global' into the file of the user and never took it back, so the second run of the check read that rule and decided by the state of the machine; the file of the check and the runner of the checks belong to the owner, and the owner repaired both (the runner gives every check a configuration of its own, and the check takes its rules back at the end).
refuted_by: A scope has no carrier or two carriers, a rule is written into the carrier of another scope, a rule that is saved in a file is never read back, or a scope that holds no rule is accepted.
note: The wave is the second of the track C (the areas of the approval): the core (C1), the carriers (C2) and the surfaces (C3).  (1) **The decisions of the parent are named and dated** (2026-11-22): every scope has exactly one carrier and the table `yeah-perm--carriers' is the one place of the correspondence; the scope `once' holds no rule and a rule that carries it is refused by name; the scope `run' is the memory of the run; the scope `session' is the memory of the ACP session; the scope `project' is `<project-root>/.yeah/rules.json'; the scope `global' is `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/yeah/rules.json' and `~/.config/yeah/rules.json' when the variable of the environment is not set; a rule of a scope lands in the carrier of that scope and in no other; the format of the file is JSON; a file that is not there is a file of no rules, a file that is broken is a refusal that names the file and the reason; the write is atomic; the paths come from one place.  (2) **The measurement is a real move**: the check of the wave (482 lines) writes a rule into a file of a carrier in a temporary directory and reads it back, and it plays the three paths -- the person, the run and the session -- and reads where the rule landed.  (3) **The control bites** (measured by the writer): `sed -i 's|(let ((file (funcall (nth 3 entry))))|(let ((file (yeah-perm--user-rules-file)))|' lib/yeah-perm.el' makes the check fail with its own assertion `the rule of the project landed in the file of the user'.  (4) **The wave found the defect of the hermeticity of a check of another wave** and named it; the owner repaired the check and the runner of the checks, and the repair is measured: three runs of the check of the approvals in a row are green and the file of the user is not written, and the control of the repair (the reset that takes the rules back is broken) makes the check fail with `the check left a rule in the file of the user behind'.  (5) **The wave moved two references of the picture of the layers** (`lib/yeah-perm.el' and `lib/yeah-acp.el'); the picture belongs to the owner and the owner re-binds the anchors when the track C is in the tree.
